clue.text: Viciously beat staff, incorporating a way to learn: It's good for you, supposedly

indicators.note: a vicious beating knocks things about, so the word beat is battered out of its order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take something into your body, so one word swallows another

parts.note: a cane is a walking staff or stick
learning by rote means by repetition

explanation.surface: A thug beats a member of staff and learns a lesson, and the clue ends with a wry claim that this is wholesome.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon hides the join: everything before it is wordplay. 'Supposedly' hedges because the health claims for the supplement are debated.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta-carotene is the orange pigment in carrots, sold as a dietary supplement and widely promoted as healthy.

clue.text: "No shoes!"—an official interrupts kick

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so these letters sit inside the other word

parts.note: to boot is to kick
the indefinite article
a ref, short for referee, is a match official

explanation.surface: A referee breaks into a kickabout shouting that no footwear is allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted 'No shoes!' looks like a sign or command, but it is the definition read as a description.
explanation.definitionFit: Going barefoot means wearing nothing on the feet, the state of having no shoes.

clue.text: No shirt, looking up notice about the French

indicators.note: about means around, so this word goes round the next piece
in a down clue looking up means reading from the bottom to the top

parts.note: to spot is to notice
les is the French plural definite article

explanation.surface: A sign seen when looking up says shirtless customers won't be served, in French.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the turned word reads upward, and the French article sits inside it rather than after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Topless means without any clothing on the upper body, so having no shirt on.

clue.text: No service here (California party with uplifting atmosphere)

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
a fete is a festive gathering

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting something up means reading it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: air is the atmosphere around us

explanation.surface: Californians throw a cheerful party where nobody is served.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: there is no table service because diners fetch their own food.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service restaurant, so customers serve themselves rather than being waited on.

clue.text: Soars in emergencies, almost from the beginning

indicators.note: this says the word is nearly complete but cut short at its start, losing its first letter

parts.note: crises are emergencies

explanation.surface: Something shoots up whenever emergencies arise, and nearly always from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost from the beginning' reads like a time phrase, but it means lop off the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise is to go upwards, and soaring is climbing high in the air.

clue.text: I cut a tram in pieces — disturbing!

indicators.note: smashed into pieces, the letters can be reassembled in a different order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to sawing a tram into pieces, which is upsetting.
explanation.definitionFit: Traumatic experiences cause deep emotional distress, so they are disturbing.

clue.text: Forbids fornication in flip-flops

indicators.note: a flip-flop is a complete turnaround, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: fornication is sex outside marriage
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puritan bans sex while wearing beach sandals, or a politician keeps changing position on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal but supplies its own two letters before the whole lot is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To nix something is informal American usage for refusing or vetoing it.

clue.text: Actress Ruby has permit to strike

indicators.note: having something means holding it, so these letters go inside the name

parts.note: Ruby Dee was an American stage and screen actress
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: An actress holds a permit allowing her to go on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' looks like industrial action, but here it means strike out text.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike a word or passage is to cross it out, which is to delete it.

clue.text: Initially, New York election trickster is no Russian

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letters of the words that follow

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A crooked operator meddling in a New York election turns out not to be Russian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No Russian' reads as 'not a Russian' but means the Russian word for no.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyet is the Russian word for no, familiar from Cold War reporting.

clue.text: Failing dandy invested in knight's regressive scams

indicators.note: regressing means going backwards, so the whole string is read from its end
money invested in something is put inside it, so these letters go within another word

parts.note: the title a knight holds
a fop is a vain, overdressed man
F is the failing grade in American schools

explanation.surface: A dandy down on his luck gets drawn into a knight's crooked schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing' looks like an adjective for the dandy but is just the letter F; the inserted letters go after the knight's first letter before everything is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rip-off is a swindle or fraud, so rip-offs are scams in everyday slang.

clue.text: Even one enclosure for eleven alien butterflies

indicators.note: an enclosure is a pen that surrounds what it holds, so one word wraps around the others

parts.note: as in 'not even one' = 'not any'
Roman numeral for eleven
the extraterrestrial of the film E.T.

explanation.surface: A collector puts some exotic alien butterflies in a single cage for a team of eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butterflies' looks like the insects but means the nervous feeling in the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Having butterflies in your stomach is an idiom for nervousness, so the word is a fair synonym for worry.

clue.text: Radical left embracing empty warships

indicators.note: an embrace wraps arms around someone, so one piece holds another inside it
radical change rips things up by the roots, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
E marks empty on a fuel gauge

explanation.surface: Radical leftists welcome a navy whose ships have nothing on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical left' reads as a political phrase, but 'Radical' is only the signal to rearrange the word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleet is a navy's body of ships operating together, so it stands for warships as a group.

clue.text: Reversing durations (including second and minute) can be somewhat bitter

indicators.note: to include is to hold within, so the next two pieces sit inside the turned word
reversing a word means running its letters back to front

parts.note: times are lengths or durations
S is the abbreviation for second
minute pronounced my-NEWT means tiny, and wee means small

explanation.surface: Thinking back over the passing of time, seconds and minutes included, can leave one feeling a little bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second and minute' look like units of time going with 'durations', but minute is the adjective meaning tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Semisweet chocolate is dark chocolate with only a little sugar, so it keeps a noticeable bitter edge.

clue.text: Perceptive butler, say, pursues uninitiated task

indicators.note: someone uninitiated has not been let in at the start, so the word loses its opening letter
to pursue is to follow behind, so this piece comes after the other one

parts.note: a job is a task
a butler is one example of a servant, as 'say' signals

explanation.surface: A sharp-eyed butler follows behind a novice who has a chore to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butler, say' marks an example: the butler stands for the broader class of domestic staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone observant notices things quickly, which is what perceptive describes.

clue.text: Love kerfuffle over allowance

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting over another is simply placed first

parts.note: ado is a fuss or commotion
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: A lovers' row breaks out over how much one partner is allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' looks like a tennis score or a term of address, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep, worshipful affection, a strong synonym for love as a noun.

clue.text: Understands, forward and backward

indicators.note: a word that reads the same in both directions is a palindrome

parts.note: as in 'I see what you mean'

explanation.surface: Someone grasps a matter thoroughly, going over it both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue simply adds that the answer reads the same either way, a hint for solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: To see a point is to grasp it, so sees means comprehends in the everyday idiom.

clue.text: Recombine elements of lady's youth

parts.note: a salad is a dish of separate ingredients tossed together

indicators.note: to recombine is to put the parts together again in a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A biology lesson on recombining the genetic elements of a woman's youth.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the wordplay does not quite work: rearranging LADYS leaves a spare L once DAYS is formed. The phrase comes from Shakespeare's Cleopatra: 'my salad days, when I was green in judgment.'
explanation.definitionFit: Salad days is an idiom for the inexperienced, carefree period of early life.

clue.text: Cyrus follows the best study habit

indicators.note: follows says this piece comes after the others in the answer

parts.note: ten is a perfect score, as in a perfect 10
a den is a small private room, a study
Cy is the short form of the name Cyrus

explanation.surface: A man named Cyrus copies the best student's way of studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study habit' looks like one phrase, but the two words do different jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency is an inclination to behave a certain way, which is what a habit is.

clue.text: Retracted commercials for 22's movement

indicators.note: retracting draws something back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: two ads, AD plus AD

explanation.surface: An advertiser pulls commercials made for a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 22 is the painter Max Ernst, a leading member of this art movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Dada was the early twentieth-century anti-art movement to which Ernst belonged before Surrealism.

clue.text: Eccentric bards captivating university, like much of 17

indicators.note: to captivate is literally to hold captive, so one letter is held inside the others
eccentric means off-centre and odd, so these letters are set out in an unusual order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Odd poets charm a campus, the way avant-garde artists do.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is DADA, the art movement famed for nonsense works.
explanation.definitionFit: Dada art was deliberately nonsensical and irrational, so absurd describes much of it.

clue.text: Vibrate broken coils at the 11th hour

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces that can be put back together differently

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
the eleventh hour means the last possible moment, late

explanation.surface: Broken springs start to rattle at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coils at' looks like anagram material, but only coils is rearranged; 'at the 11th hour' is one idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: To oscillate is to swing back and forth regularly, the motion of something vibrating.

clue.text: Announce a check charge

indicators.note: announcing is saying out loud, so the answer is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a rein checks a horse, so a check is 'a rein'

explanation.surface: Someone declares that a fee is being added to the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: In American usage check also suggests a restaurant bill, which is the surface's misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to formally call an accused person before a court to answer a criminal charge.

clue.text: Pay no attention to turning down angry person's primal urge

indicators.note: turning round makes the whole string face the other way, read from end to start

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for down in crossword grids
a rager is someone in a rage, plus the possessive S
the id is Freud's term for the instinctive drives

explanation.surface: Advice to ignore an angry person's baser instincts while refusing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning down' reads as rejecting, but 'turning' signals the reversal and 'down' is just D.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard something is to ignore it or give it no heed.

clue.text: Socialist socialites

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Eugene V. ..., the American socialist leader and presidential candidate
second meaning: short for debutantes, young women entering high society

explanation.walkthrough: The two near-identical words point to opposite ends of society, one a labour leader, the other society girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Debs was a famous American socialist, and debs is also the plural of the colloquial short form of debutante.

clue.text: 17 and I abandon painters in disarray, leaving a participant in 17

indicators.note: disarray is disorder, so what remains is jumbled
to abandon is to leave behind, so those letters drop out of the word

parts.note: 17 is DADA, and dada is a childish word for father, PA
taken as written
the word from which the letters are removed

explanation.surface: The movement and I walk out on the painters, leaving them in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is reading 17 not as the movement but as the baby-talk word for father, so PA and I come out of PAINTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst, the German painter, was a leading figure of Dada in Cologne before turning to Surrealism.

clue.text: Alternately drew in some belief system

indicators.note: alternately means every other one, so only the odd letters are kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: Someone takes turns sketching parts of a religious creed.
explanation.definitionFit: Deism is the belief in a creator god who does not intervene, a religious philosophy or creed.

clue.text: Yes, Russian favoring Republicans was brazen

parts.note: da is Russian for yes
in US electoral maps Republican-leaning states are coloured red

explanation.surface: A Russian brazenly backs the Republicans, an apparent jab at politics.
explanation.walkthrough: Red usually suggests the left, but in American election maps it marks Republican states.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dared acted with boldness or audacity, which is what being brazen means.

clue.text: I can be found after friend, taking jog in African country

indicators.note: coming after places this piece at the end
taking something in means holding it inside

parts.note: bud, from buddy, is a friend
a jog is a gentle run
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller says they can be found jogging with a friend in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Burundi is a small landlocked nation in East Africa, bordering Rwanda and Tanzania.

clue.text: Brad, with a note written backward in foreign language

indicators.note: writing backward means putting the letters down from the last to the first

parts.note: a brad is a small thin nail
taken as written
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Brad, perhaps an actor, writes a note in a foreign script.
explanation.walkthrough: Brad looks like a man's name (Pitt, say), but it is a type of nail.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian is the language of Italy, foreign to an English-speaking solver.

clue.text: Building trade's last word taken back by boy featured in tale

indicators.note: something featured in a story appears inside it, so it is placed within

parts.note: a tale is a story; it holds the other pieces

indicators.note: taking words back means retracting them, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: amen is the final word of a prayer
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: In a story, a boy retracts the final word on how the building trade works.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Building trade' is a link meaning 'is'. 'Last word' is the closing word of a prayer, not anything to do with trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonemasonry, cutting and laying stone, is one of the construction crafts.
